brief.headline: Force Claude Code to prove its work before it stops
brief.summary:
The strongest tonight-actionable items are two plugins that turn Claude Fable 5's think/act/prove loop into something any model can run: fablize wraps Opus in a completion-evidence-verification procedure, and fable-method ships the same pattern as installable skills plus an eval. Pair either with ponytail to bias agents toward the smallest diff, and update claude-code-router to 3.0.22 for prompt_cache_key forwarding on openai_responses — a direct cut on cached or routed call costs. CopilotKit's OpenBot adds a complementary pattern for browser-touching subagents: every action needs approval before it runs and gets logged after, which is what actually makes an overnight run reviewable.

On spend, several new proxies landed at once: opencodex and Fuxi both route Claude Code or Codex traffic to Ollama, DeepSeek, or other cheap backends, devspace tries to drive an agent loop off an existing ChatGPT/Claude web login instead of API billing, and kimi-k3-in-c runs a 2.78T-parameter model on a single CPU in 8GB RAM as a free backend for low-stakes background tasks. Don't lean too hard on the subscription route, though — OpenAI just restored the 5-hour Codex/Work cap on ChatGPT Plus, so a Plus login is no longer a safe stand-in for unlimited overnight compute. For managing the resulting sprawl of concurrent sessions, omnigent gives one policy/sandbox layer across harnesses with remote control, and nodeterm gives you a visual tmux-backed canvas for the same thing.
bullets: Install fivetaku/fablize or clone Sahir619/fable-method to force evidence and verification before an agent marks a task done
Install DietrichGebert/ponytail to bias agents toward minimal diffs, so morning PRs are smaller and easier to review
Update claude-code-router to 3.0.22 for prompt_cache_key forwarding on openai_responses, a direct cost cut on cached or routed calls
Clone lidge-jun/opencodex or fuxicodex/Fuxi to route background subagent calls to Ollama or DeepSeek instead of full-price API
Wire CopilotKit/OpenBot's approve-then-log action loop into a browser-touching subagent for an auditable overnight run
Try Waishnav/devspace against your existing Claude or ChatGPT login before adding API budget, but plan around OpenAI's reinstated 5-hour Codex/Work cap on Plus

signals.label: Proof-before-done enforcement
signals.note: fablize and fable-method both ship the same think/act/prove pattern this cycle, and OpenBot adds an approve-and-log loop for actions — verification is turning into a standard wrapper rather than a one-off prompt.

signals.label: Local and cheap-model routing tooling
signals.note: opencodex, Fuxi, devspace, and a CPU-only 2.78T model (kimi-k3-in-c) all landed in the same window, giving multiple concrete paths to keep subagent work off metered APIs.

signals.label: Subscription logins as free overnight compute
signals.note: OpenAI reinstated the 5-hour Codex/Work limit on ChatGPT Plus, undercutting the assumption that a Plus or Pro login can substitute for API budget on long unattended runs.

signals.label: Multi-harness session supervision
signals.note: omnigent and nodeterm both shipped ways to run and watch many concurrent Claude Code/Codex/Cursor sessions from one place, including remote control.

items.title: lidge-jun/opencodex — Universal provider proxy for OpenAI Codex & Claude Code — use any LLM (Claude, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek, Ollama…) with Codex CLI, App, SDK, and Claude Code
items.tldr: opencodex proxies OpenAI Codex CLI/App/SDK and Claude Code traffic to any LLM backend, including Claude, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek, and local Ollama models.
items.whyItMatters: Lets you route expensive subagent calls to cheaper or local models without changing your Claude Code or Codex workflow.
items.tryThis: Clone lidge-jun/opencodex and point a background subagent at an Ollama or DeepSeek endpoint instead of full-price API calls.

items.title: cobusgreyling/loop-engineering — Practical patterns, starters & CLI tools for loop engineering with AI coding agents. Design systems that prompt and orchestrate agents (inspired by Addy Osmani and Boris Cherny). Includes loop-audit, loop-in
items.tldr: loop-engineering ships CLI tools (loop-audit, loop-init, loop-cost) for designing and orchestrating long-running AI coding agent loops.
items.whyItMatters: Gives concrete commands for auditing agent loops and tracking their spend, directly addressing unattended-run reliability and cost.
items.tryThis: Clone cobusgreyling/loop-engineering and run loop-init to scaffold an audited agent loop, then loop-cost to track spend.

items.title: fivetaku/fablize — A Claude Code plugin that makes Opus behave like Fable — completion, evidence, and verification enforced as procedure. Ships only what a Fable-vs-Opus comparison proved transferable.
items.tldr: fablize is a Claude Code plugin that forces Opus to follow a completion-evidence-verification procedure modeled on Claude Fable 5.
items.whyItMatters: Directly targets unattended runs that end with unverified 'done' claims — the plugin makes the agent prove its work before stopping.
items.tryThis: Install fivetaku/fablize as a Claude Code plugin and turn on its verification procedure for long unattended sessions.

items.title: DietrichGebert/ponytail — Makes your AI agent think like the laziest senior dev in the room. The best code is the code you never wrote.
items.tldr: ponytail is a prompt/config tool that pushes an AI coding agent to write the minimum code needed, like a lazy senior dev.
items.whyItMatters: Directly targets over-engineered, bloated diffs — the opposite of what you want waiting in a morning PR review.
items.tryThis: Install DietrichGebert/ponytail and wire its prompt into a hook or skill to bias agents toward the smallest possible diff.

items.title: omnigent-ai/omnigent — Omnigent is an open-source AI agent framework and meta-harness: orchestrate Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Pi, and custom agents — swap harnesses without rewriting, enforce policies and sandboxing, and collaborate in rea
items.tldr: Omnigent is an open-source meta-harness that orchestrates Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Pi, and custom agents under one policy/sandboxing layer, controllable from any device.
items.whyItMatters: Gives one place to enforce sandboxing across harnesses and lets you check in on or steer overnight agents from your phone.
items.tryThis: Install omnigent-ai/omnigent and wire your existing Claude Code sessions through it for shared sandboxing policy and remote access.

items.title: FareedKhan-dev/kimi-k3-in-c — A 2.78-trillion-parameter Kimi K3 running inference on a single CPU in 8.24 GB of RAM. Portable C99: no BLAS, no framework, no GPU.
items.tldr: kimi-k3-in-c runs the 2.78T-parameter Kimi K3 model on a single CPU in 8.24GB RAM, in portable C99 with no BLAS, framework, or GPU.
items.whyItMatters: A frontier-scale model now runs on ordinary CPU-only hardware, so you can offload background subagent work without a GPU box.
items.tryThis: Clone FareedKhan-dev/kimi-k3-in-c and benchmark it as a free, CPU-only backend for low-stakes background subagent tasks.

items.title: Waishnav/devspace — Turn ChatGPT into Codex! OR Turn Claude Web into Claude Code!
items.tldr: devspace wraps a ChatGPT or Claude web session so it drives a Codex-like or Claude Code-like agent loop instead of billed API calls.
items.whyItMatters: Turns an existing Plus/Pro subscription into a coding-agent backend, cutting per-token API spend for overnight runs.
items.tryThis: Try Waishnav/devspace against your Claude Pro or ChatGPT Plus login before adding more API budget for unattended runs.

items.title: CopilotKit/OpenBot — Open-source AI coworkers that each get a computer of their own: a browser, files and tools, with every action decided before it happens and recorded after. Bring any AG-UI agent.
items.tldr: CopilotKit's OpenBot gives any AG-UI agent its own browser and files, gating every action for approval before it runs and logging it after.
items.whyItMatters: The pre-action approval and post-action log is a concrete pattern for making unattended agent runs auditable, which is what turns an overnight run into something you can actually review in the morning.
items.tryThis: Clone CopilotKit/OpenBot and wire an existing AG-UI agent to its action-approval/recording loop to test an unattended browser task.

items.title: Sahir619/fable-method — The Fable Workflow: how Claude Fable 5 worked, distilled into skills any model can run, with the eval that keeps it honest. Think / act / prove.
items.tldr: fable-method distills the workflow behind Claude Fable 5 into portable skills plus an eval, forcing a think / act / prove cycle on any model.
items.whyItMatters: Gives you a drop-in verification loop that catches an agent's unproven claims before you're the one reviewing the PR.
items.tryThis: Clone Sahir619/fable-method and install its skills so agents must produce evidence before marking work done.

items.title: eneskirca/nodeterm — Node-based terminal manager for AI coding agents — tmux-backed terminals and parallel agent sessions as draggable nodes on an infinite pan/zoom canvas. macOS, Linux, and a browser Server Edition.
items.tldr: nodeterm is a tmux-backed terminal manager that runs parallel AI coding agent sessions as draggable nodes on an infinite pan/zoom canvas, for macOS, Linux, and browser.
items.whyItMatters: Directly fits a worktree-and-subagent workflow: a visual way to track many concurrent unattended agent sessions instead of juggling tmux panes by hand.
items.tryThis: Clone eneskirca/nodeterm and point it at your existing tmux/worktree agent sessions to manage them as nodes on one canvas.

items.title: Show HN: Screen memory without screenshots, just text to Markdown
items.tldr: A macOS menu-bar app reads your focused window's text via the Accessibility API and writes one markdown log file per day, no screenshots or OCR.
items.whyItMatters: Point Claude Code at the folder to give agents real memory of what you worked on, using its bundled AGENTS.md format.
items.tryThis: Install the app, choose a log folder, and add it as a context source so Claude Code can answer 'what did I work on Tuesday.'

items.title: Pgbot: A 5.9 MB read-only Postgres tool for humans and agents
items.tldr: Pgbot is a 5.9MB read-only Postgres CLI built for both humans and AI agents to query safely.
items.whyItMatters: Gives an unattended agent a way to inspect a database overnight with zero write risk, instead of handing it full psql credentials.
items.tryThis: Add pgbot to your agent's toolset for read-only DB inspection instead of full database credentials.

items.title: v3.0.22
items.tldr: claude-code-router 3.0.22 fixes SSE multi-byte corruption, preserves provider auth/meters on import, and now forwards session id as prompt_cache_key on openai_responses.
items.whyItMatters: The prompt_cache_key forwarding is a direct cost lever for routed/cached requests, and the auth-hook fix covers the Claude Code path specifically.
items.tryThis: Update claude-code-router to 3.0.22 to get prompt_cache_key forwarding on openai_responses and the Claude Code local-agent auth fix.

items.title: llm-anthropic 0.27
items.tldr: Simon Willison ships llm-anthropic 0.27 for the anthropic v1.0 SDK migration, and shows the exact Claude Code prompt he used to make an agent do the upgrade and open the PR.
items.whyItMatters: It's a working template for handing an agent a migration guide URL and a test-passing bar, then reviewing the resulting PR cold.
items.tryThis: Reuse the pattern: prompt Claude Code with 'read <migration guide URL> and get the tests passing' for your own dependency bumps.

items.title: oomol-lab/open-connector — Open-source auth gateway connecting 1000+ SaaS providers to AI agents through SDK, CLI, MCP, HTTP, and OpenAPI.
items.tldr: open-connector is a self-hostable auth gateway connecting agents to 1000+ SaaS providers over MCP, SDK, CLI, HTTP, or OpenAPI.
items.whyItMatters: Saves you from hand-rolling OAuth for every tool an unattended agent needs to touch, like calendars or notification services.
items.tryThis: Self-host oomol-lab/open-connector and expose it as an MCP server for the SaaS tools your agents already need.

items.title: fuxicodex/Fuxi — FuXi is a fast, self-contained AI coding agent that lives in your terminal — edit code, run commands, and drive tools, with cost-aware routing across LLM providers.
items.tldr: FuXi is a terminal coding agent with built-in cost-aware routing across multiple LLM providers.
items.whyItMatters: It's a working reference implementation for routing subagent work to cheaper models instead of building that routing logic from scratch.
items.tryThis: Clone fuxicodex/Fuxi and inspect its provider-routing config for a pattern to send cheap subagent tasks to lower-cost models.

items.title: larlarua/AutoCVE — Agent-driven automated CVE discovery platform for source code auditing, vulnerability verification, and report generation.
items.tldr: AutoCVE is an agent-driven pipeline that audits source code, verifies discovered vulnerabilities, and generates CVE reports automatically.
items.whyItMatters: Could run overnight as a security-review subagent ahead of merging a PR, surfacing verified vulnerabilities before you look at the diff.
items.tryThis: Clone larlarua/AutoCVE and point it at a repo to get a verified vulnerability report ready for your morning PR review.

items.title: lexmount/moli — Best headless browser for AI agents. Lite, Fast, High-Compatibility. Built in Rust
items.tldr: moli is a new Rust-built headless browser designed specifically for AI agents, pitched as lighter and faster than existing options.
items.whyItMatters: A faster, more compatible browser backend could replace Puppeteer/Playwright in an agent's tool-use loop for overnight web-verification steps.
items.tryThis: Swap your agent's browser tool for lexmount/moli and benchmark startup time and page-compat against your current driver.

items.title: OpenAI restores 5-hour Codex and Work limits for ChatGPT Plus users
items.tldr: OpenAI reinstated the 5-hour usage windows for Codex and Work limits on ChatGPT Plus.
items.whyItMatters: If you lean on a Plus subscription for overnight Codex runs, your session window is capped again — plan long runs around the reset.
items.tryThis: Check your ChatGPT Plus Codex usage window before scheduling long overnight runs, and split work into sub-5-hour chunks if needed.

items.title: v1.18.23
items.tldr: OpenCode v1.18.23 fixes Cloudflare AI Gateway routing for third-party providers and corrects Anthropic model-slug conversion (e.g. claude-haiku-4.5).
items.whyItMatters: If Claude calls are routed through Cloudflare AI Gateway for cost control, this fix unblocks that path; it also fixed a parent-session-ID header bug affecting session-aware providers.
items.tryThis: Upgrade OpenCode to v1.18.23 if you route Claude models through Cloudflare AI Gateway.

items.tldr: Claude Code 2.1.245 fixes a startup crash on Linux distros shipping glibc 2.44, including Arch, CachyOS, and Fedora Rawhide.
items.whyItMatters: If you run Claude Code on a rolling-release Linux box, this is the fix that unblocks it.
items.tryThis: Update Claude Code to 2.1.245 if it won't start on Arch, CachyOS, or Fedora Rawhide.

clusters.title: Fable 5's workflow distilled into enforceable plugins
clusters.summary: Two separate projects this cycle package the same think/act/prove verification loop from Claude Fable 5 into a form any model can run, aimed squarely at unattended runs that end in an unproven 'done.'

clusters.title: Routing subagent work off metered APIs
clusters.summary: A cluster of proxies and runnable models — a Codex/Claude Code provider proxy, a cost-aware terminal agent, a subscription-login wrapper, and a CPU-only 2.78T model — all give ways to move background agent work to cheaper or free compute.

clusters.title: Supervising many concurrent agent sessions
clusters.summary: Omnigent adds a shared policy and sandboxing layer with remote control across harnesses, while nodeterm gives a visual tmux-backed canvas for the same multi-session sprawl.
